title: fallback-orchestrator: gating fast-path kernels and safe precision fallback for continuous batching
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: continuous batching and kernel selection yield large perf wins but expose correctness risk when mixed-precision kernels and KV-cache corner cases interact. This PR introduces a fallback orchestrator that gates the fast path (optimized kernels + speculative scheduling) and gracefully falls back to a safe-mode execution when heuristics detect precision instability or KV cache mismatch. Summary of changes: 1) fastpath gating layer: lightweight runtime hook that evaluates a per-request heuristic (sequence length variance, kv-hit-ratio, requested precision) and routes to 'fast' or 'safe' execution. 2) kernel_selector: new scoring to prefer stable kernels for paths flagged as 'safe' and aggressive low-precision kernels for 'fast'. 3) kv_cache: additional validation pass and a compact mismatch detector that triggers safe-mode without invalidating the whole cache. 4) continuous_batcher: batching policy extension to allow heterogeneous batches where safe and fast items can co-reside with confined isolation; introduces a micro-batch spill to preserve latency SLOs. 5) config: precision_profile and runtime flags to tune gating sensitivity and to force safe-mode for debugging. Design tradeoffs: the gating heuristic is conservative by default (prioritizes correctness) but exposes a tunable curve for teams willing to trade correctness margins for throughput. Performance: on internal Llama-2-13B evaluation the fast-path increases throughput by ~28% and reduces p95 token latency by ~12% for homogeneous workloads; mixed workloads saw a 9-15% throughput gain with negligible correctness regressions when heuristics tuned. Testing: unit tests for selector and cache detector, integration tests that run end-to-end with BFloat16/FP16 toggles, and a stress bench that simulates cache churn. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `runtime.fallback_orchestrator.enabled`; staged rollout to Dedicated pools then Hosted, with telemetry gating and a rollback switch. Related: ENG-1479, ENG-1534. This description is a single continuous string and includes design notes, tradeoffs, and rollout instructions.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Overall approach looks solid. Can we make the gating heuristic pluggable so teams can replace it with model-specific signals?
Author (Asha Patel): Yes, the orchestrator exposes a trait and a registration point; added an example in docs and tests to show swapping heuristics.
Olivia Chen: The heterogeneous micro-batching is clever but worried about head-of-line blocking under pathological mixes; do we have a backpressure strategy?
Author (Asha Patel): Added micro-batch spill and a per-queue token budget to bound latency impact; included stress bench results in perf tests.
Benji Kumar: kv_cache mismatch detector must not be a silent invalidation — add metrics and a non-destructive debug mode.
Author (Asha Patel): Implemented non-destructive validation and telemetry; added fallback_metrics for ops to trace incidents.
CI Bot: perf-regression check reported +3% on a narrow synthetic; please confirm this is acceptable for initial rollout.
Author (Asha Patel): Confirmed; added a tuning guide and default is conservative. We will gate by telemetry for Hosted rollout.
release_notes: Introduce fallback orchestrator to gate fast-path kernels and provide a safe-mode fallback for continuous batching; add tunable precision profiles and KV cache validation; default conservative settings prioritize correctness; rollout behind feature flag and telemetry.
